about: Contratto is one of the historic houses of Canelli, the Piedmont town that gave Italy its sparkling Moscato. Giuseppe Contratto founded the firm in 1867, and beginning in 1899 the company spent about ten years hand-digging cellars more than thirty metres into the hillside beneath its Art Nouveau headquarters. Canelli’s “underground cathedrals” are now part of the UNESCO-listed vineyard landscape of Piedmont. Since 2011 Contratto has belonged to Giorgio Rivetti and his brothers of La Spinetta, who revived the aperitivi and digestivi the house had stopped making in the late 1960s.

The fernet draws on thirty-three herbs, spices, roots and seeds, among them aloe, myrrh, saffron, rhubarb, quassia, anise, fennel, ginger, mint, juniper, nutmeg, clove and milk thistle. The botanicals are milled and cold-macerated for more than thirty-five days, then combined with an organic distillate of Italian wheat made in Cuneo. The blend is sweetened with beet sugar, coloured with natural caramel, chilled, slowly filtered to remove every solid, and rested about forty days in stainless steel before bottling at 30% alcohol.

At about 60 grams of sugar per litre it sits between a bone-dry bitter and a sweet amaro. Its importer’s tasting note picks out chamomile and saffron among the bitter roots and resins, a gentler profile than the menthol-forward fernets many guests know. It is an after-dinner pour, taken neat or over a single cube.
facts: Cold maceration 35+ days; rested ~40 days in stainless steel
title: Contratto Fernet
